notes: Japanese particles and first verbs for the Grammar Learner. Written for this project.
Examples are [Japanese, romaji, English]; {braces} mark the particle.
Drills are { q, en, options, answer, why }; ＿ is the blank.

Lessons and planned points are leveled by the JLPT stage they're usually taught for: N5 is absolute-beginner or beginner, N4 beginner-intermediate, N3 intermediate, N2 advanced-intermediate and N1 advanced. The plan is written for this project from the commonly taught JLPT grammar points; no text is taken from a source.
title: Japanese particles and first verbs
intro: Particles are short words that come after a noun and tell you its job in the sentence: topic, subject, object, place, time, and so on. Japanese word order is flexible because the particles carry that information. After the particles come です, polite verbs with ます in the present and past, the two kinds of adjective, and requests with てください. Each lesson has a short explanation, examples and a drill.

lessons.title: は — the topic
lessons.summary: Marks what the sentence is about. Written は, said “wa”.

sections.p: は sets the topic: “as for X, …”. Everything after it is a comment about X. It is written with the hiragana は (ha) but pronounced wa when it is a particle.
examples: わたし{は}がくせいです。
I am a student. (As for me, student.)
It's hot today. (As for today, hot.)

sections.p: は also contrasts one thing with another: “this one, as opposed to that one”.
examples: すし{は}すきですが、さしみ{は}すきじゃないです。
Sushi wa suki desu ga, sashimi wa suki ja nai desu.
Sushi I like, but sashimi I don't.

sections.p: Once the topic is clear, Japanese leaves it out. “がくせいです” alone means “(I) am a student” when you are talking about yourself.

drills.q: わたし＿アメリカじんです。
drills.why: わたし is what the sentence is about, so it takes the topic particle は.

drills.q: これ＿なんですか。
drills.why: “As for this, what is it?” — これ is the topic.

drills.q: にほんご＿むずかしいです。
drills.why: The sentence comments on Japanese, so にほんご is the topic.

drills.q: コーヒー＿のみますが、こうちゃ＿のみません。
drills.en: I drink coffee, but I don't drink tea.
drills.why: Two things contrasted with each other both take は. (を is possible without the contrast.)

drills.q: The particle は in わたしは is pronounced…
drills.why: As a particle, は is always said “wa”.

lessons.title: が — the subject
lessons.summary: Points at who or what does something, especially new information.

sections.p: が marks the grammatical subject: the one who does the action or has the quality. Use it when the subject is new to the conversation, or is the answer to “who?” or “what?”.
A question word like だれ (who) or なに (what) can never be the topic, because it is the unknown. It takes が, and so does the answer.
examples: たなかさん{が}きました。

sections.p: With すき (liked), きらい (disliked), じょうず (good at), へた (bad at), わかる (understand) and ほしい (want), the thing liked or understood takes が.
examples: にほんご{が}わかります。

drills.q: だれ＿きましたか。
drills.why: Question words like だれ are new information and take が, never は.

drills.q: こうえんにいぬ＿います。
drills.en: There is a dog in the park.
drills.why: The dog is introduced as new information: “a dog exists”.

drills.q: わたしはテニス＿すきです。
drills.why: With すき, the thing you like takes が.

drills.q: かんじ＿わかりますか。
drills.why: わかる takes が for the thing understood.

drills.q: あめ＿ふっています。
drills.why: Rain is the subject doing the falling, described as a new event.

sections.p: A rule of thumb: は points at what you are talking about and stresses what comes after it; が stresses the word before it.
examples: I'll do it. (As for me, I'll do it.)
I'll do it. (Me, not someone else.)

sections.p: は can set a big topic and が a smaller subject inside it.
examples: ぞう{は}はな{が}ながいです。
Zō wa hana ga nagai desu.
Elephants have long trunks. (As for elephants, the trunk is long.)
わたし{は}あたま{が}いたいです。
Watashi wa atama ga itai desu.
I have a headache. (As for me, the head hurts.)

drills.q: A: だれがせんせいですか。 B: やまださん＿せんせいです。
drills.en: Who is the teacher? — Ms. Yamada is.
drills.why: The answer to a “who?” question is the new information, so it takes が.

drills.q: やまださん＿せんせいです。(introducing her job)
drills.why: Ms. Yamada is the topic; the new information is “teacher”.

drills.q: うさぎはみみ＿ながいです。
drills.why: うさぎ is the big topic (は); みみ is the subject of ながい inside it (が).

drills.q: きのう、ふしぎなこと＿ありました。
drills.why: A new event being introduced takes が.

lessons.title: を — the object
lessons.summary: Marks what the action is done to. Said “o”.

sections.p: を marks the direct object: the thing eaten, read, bought, seen. It is pronounced o; the character を is used almost only for this particle.
With verbs of movement, を marks the space you move through or leave.
examples: こうえん{を}あるきます。

drills.q: テレビ＿みます。
drills.why: テレビ is what you watch: the direct object.

drills.q: てがみ＿かきました。
drills.why: The letter is the thing written.

drills.q: はし＿わたります。
drills.why: With movement verbs, を marks the place you go across or through.

drills.q: なに＿かいましたか。
drills.why: なに is the thing bought, so it is the object.

drills.q: The particle を is pronounced…
drills.why: In standard modern Japanese を is said just like お.

lessons.title: に — time, destination, place of being
lessons.summary: A point: a time, where you go, where something is, who receives.

sections.p: Clock times, days and dates take に. Relative words like きょう (today) and あした (tomorrow) do not.
examples: にちようび{に}あいましょう。

sections.p: Where you go, come or return to.
With います and あります (to exist), the place takes に.
examples: There is a cat in the room.

sections.p: The person you give to, write to, or tell takes に.
examples: ともだち{に}てがみをかきます。
I write a letter to a friend.

drills.q: くじ＿ねます。
drills.en: I go to bed at nine.
drills.why: A clock time takes に.

drills.q: らいねんにほん＿いきます。
drills.en: I'm going to Japan next year.
drills.why: Japan is the destination.

drills.q: つくえのうえ＿ほんがあります。
drills.en: There is a book on the desk.
drills.why: With あります, the place where something exists takes に.

drills.q: せんせい＿しつもんします。
drills.en: I ask the teacher a question.
drills.why: The teacher is the one the question goes to.

drills.q: あした＿テストがあります。
drills.why: Relative time words like あした, きょう and らいしゅう take no particle.

sections.p: へ marks the direction of movement: “toward”. It is written with へ (he) but pronounced e. In most sentences you could use に instead; へ puts the weight on the journey, に on arriving.

drills.q: うち＿かえります。
drills.why: Direction of movement: へ (or に).

drills.q: The particle へ is pronounced…
drills.why: As a particle, へ is said “e”.

drills.q: きた＿むかいます。
drills.why: “Toward the north”: direction.

lessons.title: で — where it happens, how
lessons.summary: The place of an action, and the means or tool.

sections.p: Where something happens takes で. Compare に, which marks where something simply is.
examples: としょかん{で}べんきょうします。
としょかん{に}ほんがあります。
There are books in the library.

sections.p: How you do something: by train, with chopsticks, in Japanese.
examples: にほんご{で}はなしてください。

drills.q: レストラン＿ばんごはんをたべました。
drills.en: I ate dinner at a restaurant.
drills.why: Eating is an action, so the place it happens takes で.

drills.q: バス＿がっこうへいきます。
drills.en: I go to school by bus.
drills.why: The means of transport takes で.

drills.q: こうえん＿こどもがいます。
drills.en: There are children in the park.
drills.why: います only says where they are, so the place takes に.

drills.q: こうえん＿こどもがあそんでいます。
drills.en: Children are playing in the park.
drills.why: Playing is an action, so the place takes で.

drills.q: えいご＿いってください。
drills.why: The language you use is a means: で.

lessons.title: と — and, with
lessons.summary: Joins a complete list of nouns, or marks who you do something with.

sections.p: と joins nouns into a list that is complete: these things and no others.
examples: パン{と}たまごをかいました。

sections.p: The person you do something together with.
examples: ともだち{と}えいがをみます。
I'll watch a film with a friend.

drills.q: かぞく＿りょこうします。
drills.why: Doing something together with someone: と.

drills.q: ペン＿ノートがあります。(only those two)
drills.en: There is a pen and a notebook.
drills.why: と makes a complete list. や would mean “a pen, a notebook and so on”.

drills.q: わたしはやまださん＿はなしました。
drills.why: The person you talk with takes と.

lessons.title: も — also, too
lessons.summary: “Also”. Replaces は, が or を.

sections.p: も means “also” or “too”. It takes the place of は, が or を; other particles stay and も is added after them (にも, でも).
examples: わたし{も}がくせいです。
きょうと{に}{も}いきました。
I went to Kyoto as well.

sections.h: With a question word and a negative
sections.p: A question word + も + a negative verb means “not any”.
examples: なに{も}たべませんでした。

drills.q: A: わたしはにほんじんです。 B: わたし＿にほんじんです。
drills.why: “Me too”: も replaces は.

drills.q: なに＿わかりません。
drills.why: Question word + も + negative = not anything.

drills.q: おおさかに＿いきました。
drills.why: Other particles stay: に + も = にも.

lessons.title: の — of, 's
lessons.summary: Links two nouns: possession, description, “the one”.

sections.p: の joins two nouns; the first one describes or owns the second. Think “’s” or “of”, read backwards.
examples: a Japanese teacher (a teacher of Japanese)
とうきょう{の}だいがく

sections.p: When the second noun is obvious, の alone stands in for it.

drills.q: これはともだち＿かさです。
drills.why: Possession between two nouns: の.

drills.q: にほん＿くるまはたかいです。
drills.why: にほん describes くるま: “cars of Japan”.

drills.q: このかばんはだれ＿ですか。
drills.why: だれの = whose; the noun after it is left out.

lessons.title: から and まで — from, until
lessons.summary: Start and end points in time and space; から also means “because”.

sections.p: から marks a starting point, まで an end point, for both time and place.
examples: くじ{から}ごじ{まで}はたらきます。
I work from nine to five.
とうきょう{から}おおさか{まで}しんかんせんでいきます。
Tōkyō kara Ōsaka made shinkansen de ikimasu.
I go from Tokyo to Osaka by bullet train.

sections.p: After a whole clause, から gives the reason.
examples: さむい{から}、まどをしめます。
It's cold, so I'll close the window.

drills.q: がっこうは８じ＿はじまります。
drills.why: The start point is から. (に is also natural here.)

drills.q: えき＿あるきました。
drills.en: I walked as far as the station.
drills.why: The end point of the walk is まで.

drills.q: じかんがない＿、タクシーでいきます。
drills.en: There's no time, so I'll take a taxi.
drills.why: After a clause, から means “because”.

lessons.title: か, よ, ね — sentence endings
lessons.summary: Question, telling, and checking with the listener.

sections.p: Particles at the very end of a sentence set its tone. か turns a sentence into a question. よ tells the listener something they may not know. ね checks for agreement, like “isn't it?”
examples: あのみせはやすいです{よ}。
Ano mise wa yasui desu yo.
That shop is cheap, you know.

drills.q: トイレはどこです＿。
drills.why: A question ends with か.

drills.q: きょうはさむいです＿。(you both feel it)
drills.why: Seeking agreement on something you share: ね.

drills.q: あ、さいふがおちました＿！
drills.why: Telling the listener news they don't know: よ.

lessons.title: です — “to be”, politely
lessons.summary: A は B です, and its negative じゃありません.

sections.p: です (desu) ends a polite sentence that says what something is: “A は B です”. It never changes for I, you or he. Japanese has no “a” or “the”, and the topic is often left out when it is obvious.
examples: わたしはがくせい{です}。

sections.p: The negative is じゃありません (ja arimasen), or じゃないです in casual-polite speech. The past is でした (deshita).
examples: わたしはせんせい{じゃありません}。
きのうはやすみ{でした}。

drills.q: わたしはアメリカじん＿。
drills.why: A は B です: “A is B”.

drills.q: それはわたしのかさ＿。
drills.why: The polite negative of です is じゃありません.

drills.q: きのうはにちようび＿。
drills.why: The past of です is でした.

drills.q: What does 「やまださんはいしゃです」 mean?
drills.why: は marks the topic, です says “is”.

drills.q: How do you ask “Are you a student?”
drills.why: Add か to the end of the sentence.

lessons.title: Verbs with ます
lessons.summary: The polite present: does, will do, doesn't.

sections.p: Polite verbs end in ます (masu). The same form covers “I do” and “I will do”, and the verb always comes at the end. The negative swaps ます for ません (masen).
examples: まいにちコーヒーをのみ{ます}。
あしたきょうとへいき{ます}。

sections.p: Change ます to ましょう for “let's”, and to ませんか to invite someone: “won't you…?”.
examples: いっしょにたべ{ませんか}。
Would you like to eat together?

drills.q: わたしはテレビをみ＿。
drills.why: The polite present ends in ます.

drills.q: おさけはのみ＿。
drills.why: The negative of ます is ません.

drills.q: What does 「らいしゅうかえります」 mean?
drills.en: らいしゅう = next week, かえる = return
options: I won't go home next week.
drills.why: ます covers the future too; the time word says when.

drills.q: ちょっとやすみ＿。
drills.why: “Let's” is ましょう.

drills.q: えいがをみ＿か。
drills.en: Would you like to see a film?
drills.why: ませんか is a polite invitation.

lessons.title: The past: ました and ませんでした

sections.p: For the polite past, change ます to ました (mashita). For “didn't”, change it to ませんでした (masen deshita).
examples: きのうすしをたべ{ました}。
しゅくだいをし{ました}。
けさはなにもたべ{ませんでした}。
Kesa wa nani mo tabemasen deshita.
I didn't eat anything this morning.

drills.q: せんしゅうとうきょうへいき＿。
drills.en: I went to Tokyo last week.
drills.why: Something that happened: ました.

drills.q: きのうはべんきょうし＿。
drills.why: “Didn't” is ませんでした.

drills.q: What does 「よくねました」 mean?
drills.en: よく = well, ねる = sleep
drills.why: ました is the past.

drills.q: Which means “I didn't buy it”?
drills.why: ませんでした = didn't.

lessons.title: い and な adjectives
lessons.summary: Two kinds of adjectives, and how each says “not”.

sections.p: い adjectives end in い: たかい (expensive), おおきい (big). They go straight before a noun, and their negative changes い to くない: たかくないです.
examples: このへやはひろ{くない}です。
Kono heya wa hiroku nai desu.

sections.p: な adjectives such as しずか (quiet) and きれい (pretty) take な before a noun, and behave like nouns at the end: しずかです, しずかじゃありません. いい (good) is irregular: よくないです.
examples: このこうえんはきれいです。

drills.q: げんき＿こども
drills.why: げんき is a な adjective, so it takes な before a noun.

drills.q: このりんごはあま＿です。
drills.en: This apple isn't sweet. (あまい = sweet)
drills.why: An い adjective drops い and adds くない.

drills.q: Which is right? “a famous person”
drills.why: ゆうめい is a な adjective.

drills.q: The negative of いいです is…
drills.why: いい is irregular: it uses the older form よい.

drills.q: きれい is a…
drills.why: It ends in い, but it is a な adjective: きれいなへや. It is one of the few exceptions.

lessons.title: てください — please do
lessons.summary: The て form of a verb, for polite requests.

sections.p: To ask someone to do something, use the verb's て form + ください. For most verbs that end in -eru or -iru in the dictionary (たべる, みる), drop る and add て: たべて, みて.
examples: ちょっとまっ{て}ください。
ここにかい{て}ください。
ゆっくりはなし{て}ください。

sections.p: The rest change their last sound: -u, -tsu, -ru → って (まつ → まって); -mu, -bu, -nu → んで (よむ → よんで); -ku → いて (かく → かいて), with いく → いって; -su → して. する → して, くる → きて.
examples: このほんをよん{で}ください。
あしたもき{て}ください。

drills.q: ここで＿ください。
drills.why: -tsu verbs make って.

drills.q: なまえを＿ください。
drills.why: -ku verbs make いて.

drills.q: これを＿ください。
drills.why: たべる drops る and adds て.

drills.q: てがみを＿ください。
drills.why: -mu verbs make んで.

drills.q: The て form of する is…
drills.why: する is irregular: して.
